title: "Index label misuse"
index-labels:
  symbol: "Zeichen"
  see: ""
  see-also: "&nbsp;"
  symbols:
    - "Zeichen"
    - "Marken"
indexes:
  - name: notes
    title: Index of Notes
    index-labels: "siehe"
  - name: sources
    title: Index of Sources
    index-labels:
      - see: "siehe"
  - name: figures
    title: Index of Figures
    index-labels:
      separator: ""
      xref-separator: ""
  - name: strata
    title: Index of Strata
    index-labels:
      symbols: "\u200B"
      see:
        target: "vergleiche"
  - title: Index of Nothing
    index-labels:
      see: "siehe"
  - name: ""
    title: Index of the Nameless
    index-labels:
      see: "siehe"
  - name: "2nd index"
    title: Index of Bad Names
    index-labels:
      see: "siehe"
  - name: notes
    title: Index of Notes Again
    index-labels:
      see: "siehe"
filters:
  - index
---

Every `index-labels:` written in this document is written wrongly, and each
place writes a different mistake. The document's own map names a key this
extension does not print, gives a key it does print an empty value, gives
another a non-breaking space — a character a reader cannot see — and writes a
third as a list. Of the four indexes it declares, the first two write no map at
all, the first a string where a map belongs and the second a list; the third
writes a map whose two punctuation keys are both empty; and the fourth writes a
zero-width space under one key and a nested map under another. The four entries
after those are refused as declarations — one has no `name:`, one an empty one,
one a name that is no section id, and one repeats a name already declared — and
each of them writes a label map that therefore sets nothing.

So this is a document of mistakes rather than one to copy: what it demonstrates
is that each is reported where it was written, and that every word and every
mark falls back to the English one this extension has always printed.

## The first index {#site-first}

A term filing under a letter: [Osprey]{.index}. One filing under none:
[%percent]{.index}.

A cross-reference pointing at the first: [Harrier]{.index see="Osprey"}, and
one pointing further: [Goshawk]{.index see-also="Osprey"}.

## The second index {#site-second}

A term filing under a letter: [Kittiwake]{.index index="sources"}. One filing
under none: [+plussign]{.index index="sources"}.

Its own two cross-references: [Fulmar]{.index index="sources" see="Kittiwake"}
and [Petrel]{.index index="sources" see-also="Kittiwake"}.

## The third index {#site-third}

A term marked twice, so its entry carries two locators with a mark between them
as well as one in front: [Quartzite]{.index index="figures"}, and again here:
[Quartzite]{.index index="figures"}.

A term with both a locator and a cross-reference:
[Rhyolite]{.index index="figures"} and
[Rhyolite]{.index index="figures" see-also="Quartzite"}.

A term that is two cross-references, marked once for each, which is the one
place the mark between two of them is printed:
[Siltstone]{.index index="figures" see="Quartzite"} and
[Siltstone]{.index index="figures" see-also="Rhyolite"}.

## The fourth index {#site-fourth}

A term filing under a letter: [Tillite]{.index index="strata"}. One filing
under none: [=equals]{.index index="strata"}.

A cross-reference pointing at the first:
[Turbidite]{.index index="strata" see="Tillite"}.
